FROM HERE TO YOUR TERMINAL

One command.
Start creating.

Download and install CSHCLI directly from its open-source repository.

Create my first project →
PowerShell
$py -m pip install "https://github.com/jtpydk5gyh-alt/cshcli/archive/refs/heads/main.zip"

Requires Python 3.11+ with pip and the py launcher. Downloads the main branch.

1Check the installationcshcli --version
2Set up your session and projectcshcli start
3Open a conversationcshcli

If you already use a virtual environment, replace py with python.

Does Python block global installation?

Create a virtual environment and run the installation command inside it. This also avoids conflicts with other projects.

py -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\python -m pip install "https://github.com/jtpydk5gyh-alt/cshcli/archive/refs/heads/main.zip"
.venv\Scripts\cshcli --version

For the next steps, use .venv\Scripts\cshcli instead of cshcli.

Isolated installation with one command

These scripts install CSHCLI 0.7.0 from a fixed revision in a virtual environment for your user. Requires Python 3.11+; administrator permissions are not required. You can read the PowerShell script or read the shell script before running them.

Windows · PowerShell

irm https://jtpydk5gyh-alt.github.io/cshcli-web/install.ps1 | iex

macOS and Linux · Shell

curl -fsSL https://jtpydk5gyh-alt.github.io/cshcli-web/install.sh | sh

Windows adds the command to this terminal’s PATH. On macOS and Linux, it creates ~/.local/bin/cshcli; the installer tells you if you need to add that folder to PATH. It does not modify your startup configuration. The scripts pin source code by commit; a signed release has not been published yet.

BEFORE YOU TAKE OFF

Know what to expect.

Explore CSHCLI and its limits ↓
What is CSHCLI?

CSHCLI is an open-source CLI for connecting personal AI providers and coordinating projects, versioned memory, file leases and runs from the terminal. Version 0.7.0 is an alpha local pilot under the MIT license. With cshcli serve, the coordinator listens on 127.0.0.1:8765 by default. Guided setup starts a local coordinator automatically when needed. Data is stored in SQLite on your machine.

What do I need to install CSHCLI?

Requires Python 3.11 or later with pip. The basic installation adds no runtime dependencies. CLI CI covers Windows and Linux with Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13; macOS installation instructions are available, but macOS is not covered by that CI. See the commands for your system and use a virtual environment if your Python blocks global installation.

Which AI providers can I use?

CSHCLI supports the OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and MiniMax APIs with your own keys, plus adapters for the official Codex and Claude Code CLIs. Gemini CLI can be detected, but its chat remains blocked until verifiable isolation is available. Access depends on your account and a compatible provider version. See the provider status; native CSHCLI OAuth sign-in remains disabled.

Do I need an AI subscription?

CSHCLI is free to install. To query models, you need your own credentials or a supported official CLI. Access and cost depend on the provider; CSHCLI does not include credits or an AI subscription.

Can I work with a remote team yet?

This pilot lets you test multiple identities with a local coordinator. Collaboration between machines requires the remote service, which is not deployed yet. File leases are cooperative; they cannot stop an external editor from writing a file. The mediated runner validates its own writes, but does not provide a process, memory or network sandbox.

Can CSHCLI publish my applications yet?

The CLI can reserve an environment, and deployment coordination has tests using a separate process and local HTTP checks. No deployment provider is configured and no real publication has been verified yet. Read the verified project status before using it in production.

Where can I find the code and instructions?

Browse the source code, read the CSHCLI documentation, check the changelog or open an issue on GitHub. These sources describe the CLI’s current capabilities and limits.
